figures_added.what: y = 1/x plotted as two branches (x<0 and x>0); shows the horizontal asymptote y=0 the question asks the student to identify.
y = x^3 cubic, x in [-2,2]; the rising curve at x=1 lets the student see the positive gradient asked for.
y = 1/x over a wide range (x to +/-10); the positive branch visibly flattens toward the x-axis, showing y approaches 0 as x gets large.
y = -1/x as two branches; sits in the 2nd (x<0, y>0) and 4th (x>0, y<0) quadrants, matching the answer.
y = x^3 (blue) and y = -x^3 (amber) together; the pair is a mirror image in the x-axis, showing the reflection asked for.
y = 1/x (two branches) and the line y = 4x; they cross in the 1st quadrant near x=0.5. Intersection is not marked, so the exact value must still be found algebraically.
